findings.title: FeatureAgglomeration is registered as a hard clusterer but clusters FEATURES: wrong-length labels from cluster(), cryptic crash or silent 3-point plot from plot(), and a broken reuse path
findings.repro:
import numpy as np, hypertools as hyp
rng = np.random.default_rng(0)
X = np.vstack([rng.standard_normal((100, 5)) + 8.0 * i for i in range(3)])
print(len(hyp.cluster(X, cluster='FeatureAgglomeration', n_clusters=3)))  # 5, not 300
import matplotlib; matplotlib.use('Agg')
hyp.plot(X[:, :4], '.', cluster={'model': 'FeatureAgglomeration', 'n_clusters': 2}, show=False)  # 3-point figure
hyp.plot(X[:, :4], '.', cluster='FeatureAgglomeration', show=False)  # ValueError
findings.expected: Per-observation labels (docstring: 'a list of cluster labels (one per observation)'), or a clear error/warning explaining FeatureAgglomeration clusters features
findings.actual: "FeatureAgglomeration": {"type": "list", "len": 5} on (300,5) input; plot dict k=2: 'total plotted points: 3 of 300 input rows; per-artist: [1, 2]' with no warning; plot default: 'ValueError: Cannot extract more clusters than samples: 5 clusters were given for a tree with 3 leaves.'; reuse on same data: 'NotImplementedError: FeatureAgglomeration has no out-of-sample prediction ... on new data (a different number of rows than it was fit on)'

findings.title: plot(cluster='DBSCAN'|'MeanShift'|'OPTICS'|'AffinityPropagation', n_clusters=k) crashes with a cryptic constructor TypeError; only HDBSCAN gets the friendly warn-and-ignore
findings.repro:
import numpy as np, matplotlib; matplotlib.use('Agg')
import hypertools as hyp
rng = np.random.default_rng(3)
data = np.vstack([rng.standard_normal((100, 4)) + 7 * i for i in range(3)])
hyp.plot(data, '.', cluster='DBSCAN', n_clusters=3, show=False)
findings.expected: n_clusters ignored (with at most a warning), matching hyp.cluster()'s documented behavior ('Not used for models that discover the number of clusters automatically (HDBSCAN, MeanShift, DBSCAN, OPTICS, AffinityPropagation)') and plot's own HDBSCAN handling
findings.actual: TypeError: DBSCAN.__init__() got an unexpected keyword argument 'n_clusters' (identical crashes for MeanShift, OPTICS, AffinityPropagation)

findings.title: plot(random_state=) is NOT threaded to the cluster stage, contradicting the docstring; seeded cluster plots are non-reproducible
findings.repro:
import numpy as np, matplotlib; matplotlib.use('Agg')
import hypertools as hyp
noise = np.random.default_rng(3).standard_normal((120, 10))
f1 = hyp.plot(noise, '.', cluster='KMeans', n_clusters=6, random_state=0, show=False)
f2 = hyp.plot(noise, '.', cluster='KMeans', n_clusters=6, random_state=0, show=False)
# compare per-artist point sets -> differ
findings.expected: Identical cluster groupings across the two seeded calls (docstring: injected into KMeans/GaussianMixture etc.)
findings.actual: same groups across 2 seeded runs: False  -> plot(random_state=) NOT threaded to cluster= stage (docstring says it is)

findings.title: plot(cluster=..., return_model=True) without n_clusters: figure clusters with k=5 but the returned pipeline encodes k=3 -- the bundled 'exact fitted parameters' mismatch the figure
findings.repro:
import numpy as np, matplotlib; matplotlib.use('Agg')
import hypertools as hyp
rng = np.random.default_rng(3)
data = np.vstack([rng.standard_normal((100, 4)) + 7 * i for i in range(3)])
res = hyp.plot(data, '.', cluster='KMeans', return_model=True, show=False)
print(len(set(map(int, res['pipeline'].transform(data)))))  # 3, but the figure shows 5 groups
findings.expected: The returned pipeline's cluster stage uses the SAME k the figure was drawn with (5, from default_params), so pipeline.transform reproduces the plotted grouping
findings.actual: figure groups (point-artists): 5 sizes: [35, 32, 33, 100, 100]; bundle pipeline labels unique k: 3 | GaussianMixture: bundle pipeline proportions shape: (300, 3) (figure used default_params n_components=5)

findings.title: Integer cluster labels passed as hue= render clusters 0 and 1 in visually identical reds -- the shipped plot_clusters2.py example produces a single-color plot
findings.repro:
import numpy as np, matplotlib; matplotlib.use('Agg')
import hypertools as hyp
rng = np.random.default_rng(0)
data = np.vstack([rng.standard_normal((100, 3)), rng.standard_normal((100, 3)) + 3])
labels = hyp.cluster(data, n_clusters=2, random_state=0)
fig = hyp.plot(data, '.', hue=list(labels), show=False)
fc = [c for c in fig.axes[0].collections if getattr(c, '_offsets3d', None) is not None][0].get_facecolor()
print(sorted({tuple(np.round(x, 3)) for x in fc}))  # two near-identical reds
findings.expected: Visually distinct colors per cluster (the example's stated purpose: 'color our points by cluster'); string labels already behave this way
findings.actual: distinct colors: [(0.86, 0.34, 0.34, 1.0), (0.86, 0.371, 0.34, 1.0)] -- delta 0.031 in one channel; verbatim plot_clusters2.py output is a uniform red point cloud (see evidence)

findings.title: Reusing a fitted no-predict clusterer on DIFFERENT data with the SAME row count silently returns the stale fit-time labels
findings.repro:
import numpy as np, hypertools as hyp
rng = np.random.default_rng(5)
A = np.vstack([rng.standard_normal((30, 4)) + 6 * i for i in range(2)])
labels_A, model = hyp.cluster(A, cluster='AgglomerativeClustering', n_clusters=2, return_model=True)
B = rng.standard_normal((60, 4)) * 50 + 100  # unrelated data, same row count
labels_B = hyp.cluster(B, cluster=model)
print(list(labels_B) == list(labels_A))  # True, silently
findings.expected: An error (like the different-row-count case) or an explicit warning that fit-time labels are being returned and B was never actually clustered
findings.actual: labels_B == labels_A (stale fit-time labels returned for unrelated data): True; any warning raised: none (silent)

findings.title: plot(cluster=False) raises ValueError although plot's docstring documents the type as 'str, dict, False, or None'
findings.expected: No clustering applied (documented False behaves like None), or a docstring that does not list False
findings.actual: ValueError: Invalid cluster model specified; should be string or dictionary!

findings.title: Silent conflict resolution in cluster specs: an instance beats n_clusters= with no warning, and a dict carrying BOTH 'params' and 'kwargs' silently ignores 'params'
findings.repro:
import numpy as np, hypertools as hyp
from sklearn.cluster import KMeans
data = np.random.default_rng(1).standard_normal((150, 4))
print(len(set(map(int, hyp.cluster(data, cluster=KMeans(n_clusters=5, random_state=0), n_clusters=3)))))  # 5, no warning
print(len(set(map(int, hyp.cluster(data, cluster={'model': 'KMeans', 'params': {'n_clusters': 2}, 'kwargs': {'n_clusters': 4}})))))  # 4, no warning
findings.expected: A UserWarning naming the ignored setting in both cases
findings.actual: n_uniq: 5 (5 => instance wins silently) / dict with BOTH params and kwargs ... n_uniq: 4 (no warning emitted in either run)

findings.title: n_clusters precedence is inconsistent between hyp.cluster and hyp.plot: spec kwargs win in cluster(), explicit n_clusters= wins in plot()
findings.repro:
import numpy as np, matplotlib; matplotlib.use('Agg')
import hypertools as hyp
rng = np.random.default_rng(3)
data = np.vstack([rng.standard_normal((100, 4)) + 7 * i for i in range(3)])
spec = {'model': 'KMeans', 'kwargs': {'n_clusters': 2, 'random_state': 0}}
print(len(set(map(int, hyp.cluster(data, cluster=spec, n_clusters=4)))))  # 2
fig = hyp.plot(data, '.', cluster=spec, n_clusters=4, show=False)  # 4 groups
findings.expected: One consistent precedence rule (and ideally a conflict warning) across cluster() and plot()
findings.actual: hyp.cluster -> k = 2 (kwargs wins) / hyp.plot -> figure groups = 4 (explicit n_clusters wins)

findings.title: plot cluster dict without a 'model' key raises a bare KeyError; hyp.cluster gives a helpful ValueError for the same input
findings.expected: The same instructive ValueError hyp.cluster raises
findings.actual: KeyError: 'model'

findings.title: Invalid instance specs fail with cryptic AttributeErrors: cluster=42 -> "'int' object has no attribute 'fit'"; an sklearn Pipeline fits fine then dies on '.labels_'
findings.repro:
import numpy as np, hypertools as hyp
from sklearn.pipeline import Pipeline
from sklearn.preprocessing import StandardScaler
from sklearn.cluster import KMeans
X = np.random.default_rng(0).standard_normal((60, 3))
hyp.cluster(X, cluster=42)  # AttributeError: 'int' object has no attribute 'fit'
hyp.cluster(X, cluster=Pipeline([('s', StandardScaler()), ('k', KMeans(n_clusters=2, n_init=10))]))
findings.expected: A ValueError naming the accepted spec forms; ideally support fit_predict-only estimators such as sklearn Pipelines
findings.actual: RAISED AttributeError: 'int' object has no attribute 'fit' / RAISED AttributeError: 'Pipeline' object has no attribute 'labels_'

findings.title: README says 'cluster(ndims=...) arguments were removed' but cluster() still accepts ndims= -- and silently no-ops it unless reduce= is also given
findings.repro:
import numpy as np, hypertools as hyp
X = np.random.default_rng(0).standard_normal((100, 10))
a = hyp.cluster(X, n_clusters=3, ndims=2, random_state=0)
b = hyp.cluster(X, n_clusters=3, random_state=0)
print(list(a) == list(b))  # True -- ndims silently ignored
findings.expected: A warning ('ndims= has no effect without reduce=') or README/docstring accuracy about the repurposed argument
findings.actual: cluster.py line 219 gates the pipeline path on (manip, normalize, reduce, align) only; ndims-only calls take the single-stage path unchanged. README.md: 'and `cluster(ndims=...)` arguments were removed.'
